title: Ordinary nerve and internal functor simplicial sets, with parameterized evaluation
statement:
Use small ordinary nerves, standard simplices, simplicial products and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed containing universe. Let $J,I$ be small ordinary categories. The ordinary category $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{Cat}}(J,I)$ has functors as objects and natural transformations as arrows, composed componentwise. Its evaluation functor sends $(F,j)$ to $F(j)$. The map induced by the nerve of evaluation is a natural isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$\rho_{J,I}:N(\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{Cat}}(J,I))\xrightarrow{\cong}\operatorname{Fun}(N(J),N(I)).$$
Explicitly, a string $F_0\Rightarrow\cdots\Rightarrow F_r$ corresponds under $\rho_{J,I}$ to the map $N(J)\times\Delta^r\to N(I)$ obtained by taking the nerve of its evaluation functor $J\times[r]\to I$; evaluation on $(j,t)$ is $F_t(j)$, and mixed arrows use the given natural transformations. For every small simplicial set $X$, not necessarily a quasicategory, write $\operatorname{Fun}(N(J),X)$ for the simplicial set given by the same formula as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: its $n$-simplices are the simplicial maps $N(J)\times\Delta^n\to X$, and $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ acts by precomposition with $\mathrm{id}_{N(J)}\times\Delta(\alpha)$. For every simplicial map $f:N(I)\to X$, postcomposition gives a simplicial map
$$N(\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{Cat}}(J,I))\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(N(J),X).$$
The image of the displayed string is the entire prism $N(J)\times\Delta^r\to N(I)\xrightarrow{f}X$, including its faces and degeneracies. These formulas commute with restriction along every ordinary functor $q:J'\to J$ and every monotone map $\alpha:[s]\to[r]$, simultaneously: restriction of the prism is the prism of the restricted string on $J'\times[s]$. In particular, for $q:[k]\to J$ the resulting $(k,r)$-parameter prism retains all parameter faces and degeneracies, including composition faces and identity degeneracies. No invertibility of the natural transformations and no quasicategory hypothesis on $X$ is required.

proof.text: For each degree r, an r-simplex of the ordinary nerve N(Fun_Cat(J,I)) is a functor [r] → Fun_Cat(J,I). Uncurrying its objects F_t and arrows (the natural transformations between them) gives a functor E : J × [r] → I: E(j,t)=F_t(j), the J-arrows are F_t on morphisms, and the [r]-arrows are the components of the natural transformations. The naturality squares are exactly the commutation relations for mixed arrows, so this is a direct bijection of the two descriptions.

proof.text: By the degreewise definition of the internal functor simplicial set in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an r-simplex of Fun(N(J),N(I)) is a simplicial map N(J)×Δ^r→N(I). The standard simplex Δ^r is the nerve N([r]): both have m-simplices the monotone maps [m]→[r], with operators by precomposition. A functor [m]→J×[r] is a pair of functors [m]→J and [m]→[r], so N(J)×Δ^r=N(J×[r]) degreewise, compatibly with the operators. By [lem-coef-homotopy-category-nerve-adjunction], for small categories C,D there is the natural adjunction bijection Hom_Cat(τN(C),D)≅Hom_sSet(N(C),N(D)), and the counit ε_C:τN(C)→C is an isomorphism. By naturality of the counit, the map N(E) of a functor E:C→D corresponds under the adjunction to ε_D∘τN(E)=E∘ε_C. Hence E↦N(E) is the composite of the bijection E↦E∘ε_C with the adjunction bijection, and so it is a bijection Hom_Cat(C,D)→Hom_sSet(N(C),N(D)); this is Kerodon Proposition 1.3.3.1 (Tag 002Z), which the proof of Tag 0062 uses. With C=J×[r] and D=I, every r-simplex is N(E) for a unique functor E:J×[r]→I, and this decoding is inverse to the construction in the preceding step. This gives the degree-r bijection underlying ρ_{J,I}.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 1.5.3.3 (Tag 0062), proof: bijectivity of the middle map by the special case of Proposition 1.3.3.1 (Tag 002Z), full faithfulness of the nerve; read online.

proof.text: For a monotone map α:[s]→[r], precomposition on the nerve side replaces E by E∘(id_J×α), and precomposition on the internal-hom side restricts the prism along id_{N(J)}×Δ(α). These are the same operation under the two descriptions. Thus the degreewise bijections assemble to a simplicial isomorphism. The evaluation functor J×[r]→I is exactly E, so the displayed formula sends F_0⇒⋯⇒F_r to the entire prism, with mixed arrows given by the components of the natural transformations.

proof.text: Postcomposition with any simplicial map f:N(I)→X sends the prism to N(J)×Δ^r→N(I)→X and therefore defines the asserted simplicial map into Fun(N(J),X). For an ordinary functor q:J'→J, restriction is precomposition by q×id_[r] on the category side and by N(q) on the simplicial side; the square commutes degreewise. These operations commute simultaneously with α, so all parameter faces and degeneracies, including composition faces and identity degeneracies, are retained.

proof.text: The construction only uses ordinary functors, naturality equations, and the simplicial identities. It never asks a natural transformation to be invertible and never uses horn filling in X; it also works for empty J or I and for every small X. Therefore ρ is a natural isomorphism with all the stated restriction and postcomposition compatibilities.

lean.statement: theorem functorComparison_spec (J I : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [SmallCategory I] : IsIso (functorComparison J I) ∧ (∀ (X : SSet.{u}) (f : nerve I ⟶ X) (r : ℕ) (F : (nerve (J ⥤ I)) _⦋r⦌), uncurry (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm ((functorPostcompose J I f).app _ F)) = functorPrism F ≫ f) ∧ (∀ (J' : Type u) [SmallCategory J'] (q : J' ⥤ J) (X : SSet.{u}) (f : nerve I ⟶ X), nerveMap ((Functor.whiskeringLeft J' J I).obj q) ≫ functorPostcompose J' I f = functorPostcompose J I f ≫ (pre (nerveMap q)).app X) ∧ (∀ (J' : Type u) [SmallCategory J'] (q : J' ⥤ J) (X : SSet.{u}) (f : nerve I ⟶ X) (r s : ℕ) (a : ⦋s⦌ ⟶ ⦋r⦌) (F : (nerve (J ⥤ I)) _⦋r⦌), (nerveMap q ⊗ₘ SSet.stdSimplex.map a) ≫ functorPrism F ≫ f = functorPrism ((nerveMap ((Functor.whiskeringLeft J' J I).obj q)).app _ ((nerve (J ⥤ I)).map a.op F)) ≫ f) ∧ (∀ (I' : Type u) [SmallCategory I'] (g : I ⥤ I'), nerveMap ((Functor.whiskeringRight J I I').obj g) ≫ functorComparison J I' = functorComparison J I ≫ (ihom (nerve J)).map (nerveMap g))
lean.note: Canonical evaluation and prism maps are real constructions using Mathlib ordinary functor categories, evaluationUncurried, Functor.prod′, curry and ihom. The single theorem asserts the specified comparison is an isomorphism together with its full postcomposition, source restriction, simultaneous simplex restriction and target naturality formulas. No assumptions on the simplicial target or invertibility of transformations.
